claimsToVerify: Capabilities · 'Every version is reviewed before it ships' — HIGHEST RISK on this page. A publisher can install their own unreviewed version by design, so 'every version is reviewed before it ships' overstates the gate. Review lives on the version record; confirm the exact wording that is true.

Capabilities · 'an AST verifier checks each bundle against its declared network allowlist' — confirm the verifier is enforcing and not advisory (it is implemented as a lint), and that a failing bundle is actually blocked.

Capabilities · 'plugins run on a separate sandboxed origin with a per-plugin CSP' — confirm the sandbox origin and per-plugin CSP are wired for the paths this page implies; there is a realm-trust bypass to account for.

Statement, Capabilities and Hero · 'released under Apache-2.0', 'Aglyn is Apache-2.0 and public on GitHub — read the source and shape where it goes', 'Aglyn itself is built from plugins, and it’s open source' — confirm the licence is Apache-2.0 and the repo is public before this ships. Note this page makes NO self-hosting, npx create-aglyn, Kubernetes or 'no lock-in' claim, which is correct.
Capabilities · 'keep a plugin private to your own orgs until you’re ready' — confirm org-private plugin visibility exists.

Capabilities · 'Publish from a real editor with markdown READMEs and changelogs, watch your version move through review' — confirm markdown README + changelog authoring and a visible review status exist.
Capabilities · 'Seller profile & payouts — Publishers get a profile, listings, payouts, and sales — all in the console.' — confirm payouts and a sales view are actually in the console.
Deep-dive · 'every update shows the publisher’s changelog and a diff, and never overwrites your local edits' — confirm an update DIFF is shown and local edits are preserved.
Deep-dive · 'See ratings and reviews before you install.' — confirm ratings and written reviews both exist on listings.
Deep-dive and How it works · 'get paid through Stripe (Pro & up)' / '(Pro and up)' — plan-gate claim; verify the tier, and note the two spellings differ between sections.
CTA · 'build your own with the SDK' — an SDK is named only here (the capability card was renamed away from 'Plugin SDK'); confirm a documented plugin SDK exists to link to.
Hero, Capabilities and How it works · the four installable kinds 'templates, layouts, email templates, and dataset schemas' — confirm all four artifact kinds are installable today.

Capabilities · 'Commerce, bookings, email, workflows and more are plugins on the same architecture you build against.' — confirm bookings ships as a plugin and that third parties build against the same architecture.

Hero mockup (123:2695) shows a listing titled 'Leads CRM schema' — a dataset schema, not a product, but the words 'CRM schema' on a marketing page risk reading as a Contacts CRM. Consider renaming the sample listing.
Early access stats (shared across all three pages): '9 products built in' and '0 plugins to wire up' — confirm the product count.
